answer: Before the gates open the keeper sounds the chamber with a lead line, and the sounding book holds the depth for every lock on the cut. A forge chamber claimed as sounded fails the book: the lead must have dropped at the shale of the chamber, and a chamber never sounded has no depth to quote. Forging a season of soundings means bribing the keeper, faking sixty lead drops and paying 11,700, while the jetty book is read against the barges' draught marks, so a depth whose sounding was never entered grounds the boat at the sill.
